content_blocks.text: What Is Dart? matters because Dart programs need predictable behavior, explicit contracts, and examples that can be verified. This topic focuses on language characteristics, compilation, runtime, and type system. Keep the lesson’s core distinction separate from runtime, SDK, package, or platform details that may vary. When you build on this idea, state your assumptions, try the smallest useful example, and check edge cases before integrating it into a larger project.

items: Define the term in What Is Dart? and explain the boundary it introduces.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Run this file with `dart run bin/main.dart` after creating a project.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original snippet, rerun the same command, and compare the complete output. For package/platform examples, restore pubspec and target settings too.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Change one input or condition in the example for “What Is Dart?”. Predict the output first, then run or statically inspect it. Add one boundary test and explain why the result is expected.

Common mistakes: confusing a language guarantee with a runtime or package behavior; skipping malformed/empty inputs; relying on undocumented version assumptions; and changing multiple things before reproducing a failure. Prefer explicit naming, a small test, and official documentation.

content.task: Create a small, standalone Dart example that demonstrates What Is Dart?. Include a short comment naming the assumption being tested, then verify one ordinary input and one boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example focuses on the stated topic and uses clear Dart naming.
Expected behavior is documented and checked with a repeatable command or static inspection.
At least one boundary/error/platform assumption is stated.
hints: Start from the supplied minimal example and change only one behavior.
Write down the expected output before running the program.
Use `dart format .` and `dart analyze .`; add a test when the behavior matters.
